about.title: Shafter Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision takes a family member in Shafter, the days and weeks after can feel like a blur of paperwork, funeral arrangements, and unanswered questions. Kern County recorded traffic deaths on local roads recently, and behind each number is a family trying to figure out what comes next. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. These claims are separate from any criminal proceeding and typically must be filed within two years of the death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. We handle wrongful death cases and can review what happened along corridors like E Lerdo Highway or 7th Standard Road and explain what options may exist, all without any upfront cost.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with other dependents eligible only under specific circumstances. Our team can help sort out who in your family has standing before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Watching the Two-Year Clock
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a county road authority, may be involved. We work quickly to make sure that deadline isn't missed.

items.title: No Cost Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning your family owes nothing upfront and pays only if the case results in a recovery. That structure lets you focus on your family instead of legal bills.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives the surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children the first right to bring the claim. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify under specific rules. We can review your family's situation and explain who has standing.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family can pursue for financial losses and the loss of companionship. One can proceed regardless of the outcome of the other.

items.question: Does it matter that our loss happened on a road like E Lerdo Highway or Zerker Road in Shafter?
items.answer: The specific road doesn't change your legal rights, but local details like which agency maintains that corridor can affect the process and any deadlines involved. Our team is familiar with Kern County and can look into those details as part of reviewing your case.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free consultations, and we handle wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover something for your family.
